page.overview:
What is DUPLO?

Dacta DinoDollsFarmFerrariLEGO VilleLittle Forest FriendsPeppa PigPlayhousePlaypointPiratesPrimoPrincess CastleDUPLO SupplementalTilesThomas & Friends TooloTrainsTubesZootersCarsDisney PrincessDisney Jr.PlanesToy StoryWinnie the PoohFormula 1

DUPLO is a theme and a subline which was introduced as a brand in 1975, although the name and the blocks had been around since 1969. It is intended for children around 1–5 years old, and the three forms of minifigures, or DUPLO Figures are more sizable and stable, and the blocks are about twice the length, width, and height of their equivalent System brick and half the length of a QUATRO brick. It can be noted that DUPLO is compatible with normal System bricks, but only with 2x2s and further because it's too big for 1x1 and 1x2x3 bricks.

The first DUPLO bricks and the name DUPLO appeared for the first time in 1969. There were originally four colours: Red, Yellow, Blue, and White. They were designed to connect more with System bricks than the newer DUPLO bricks of recent years. The bricks were 18 times larger than a regular system brick. They were released in sets 510, and 511, both with System bricks. They were considered to be System-Duplo sets, aimed at younger children. This was the beginning of the LEGO Group's products for the younger market. Two more sets were introduced the next year, adding new blue and red wheel plates. The sets were designed for people aged 1 to 2 years old, but were continued to be mixed with System blocks. In 1972, the first 2x2 studded brick was introduced. When DUPLO/Pre-School sets were introduced in their final form in 1969, the first DUPLO sets had a green LEGO logo. This logo was short lived, and by 1971 new DUPLO sets were introduced that used the red LEGO logo, and the text 'DUPLO' in green on the box'.

In 1975, DUPLO became an independent theme, with five sets made up exclusively of DUPLO bricks. In 1977, the decision was taken to rename DUPLO Preschool. In the Preschool range, new DUPLO bricks were introduced, including arches and the first DUPLO figures, which did not have movable limbs. In 1979, the theme was returned to the name of DUPLO, and received its logo, a rabbit designed in a style similar to PRIMO's elephant.
